item.title: Intrepid, enterprising, dedicated: The new generation of nursery owners creating the flowers we'll be enjoying for decades to come
item.description: David Carver is typical of the new generation of nursery owners, determined to save historic collections and produce new hybrids. John Hoyland paid him a visit to find out more; photographs by Clive Nichols.

item.title: Hôtel du Couvent: This former convent on the French Riviera has rekindled the rules of luxury
item.description: Hôtel du Couvent has none of the excess that the French Riviera has become known for in recent years, says James Fisher.

item.title: Pushing back against a culture of disposability: The enduring importance of craft
item.description: Corrine Julius grapples with a world dominated by mass production, digital life, AI and explains why the unique and the tangible is spearheading a renaissance.

item.title: 'I do write in and say they should have more about farming': Zandra Rhodes on The Archers, getting arrested and making clothes for Freddie Mercury
item.description: Lotte Brundle meets the 85-year-old fashion designer in her vibrant apartment above the Fashion and Textile Museum in London.

item.title: Home is where the hearth is: Five picture-perfect cottages with glorious fireplaces
item.description: An imposing inglenook fireplace can be the natural heart of a home — and a characterful draw for buyers — as it radiates warmth and coaxes company towards that comforting glow.

item.title: 'I have never ceased talking of the beauty of Ampthill': The tale of one of Britain's best-loved country houses
item.description: Jeremy Musson describes the complex evolution of Ampthill Park House, Bedfordshire — home of Sir Timothy and Lady Clifford —at the hands of Sir Christopher Wren’s master mason Robert Grumbold, mason-surveyor John Lumley and Sir William Chambers.

item.title: The Shropshire boarding school that's lived multiple lives, transformed into a wonderful country house with the coolest cellar we've seen in years
item.description: Oakhurst Hall, just outside Oswestry, is a house that's lived many lives —but it's never looked better than it does now.

item.title: The revolutionary dog that almost became Ireland’s national breed
item.description: What’s the national dog of Ireland? Officially, there isn’t one — but in the early 1920s, the Kerry blue terrier came closest.

item.title: Chery Tiggo 9: Maybe the communists are onto something
item.description: A new seven-seat SUV from China has James Fisher reconsidering economic principles.

item.title: The only thing better than a stately home is a stately home in wooden miniature
item.description: Meet George Barham — the gifted woodcarver who can turn your family pile into a wooden masterpiece.
